utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Registrar, please, would you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-81, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome to this status conference, and sorry for the delay, which happened due to technical problems. We will have a telephone conference within this conference. So I first want to say my name is Frank Hoepfel, and before going into our agenda, I would like to mention, as the parties know, I am covering Judge Robinson, who is out of town due to urgent private matters which now were compounded by a death in his family. I am joining counsel who both, in yesterday's Rule 65 ter conference, expressed their condolences. Additionally, I would like to thank senior legal officer Linda Strite Murnane, who provided excellent support in providing -- in preparing for this status conference. Also, she again had yesterday's 65 ter conference. May I now have the appearances. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon. To my right is Barney Thomas, and to his right is the case manager, Carmela Javier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Hello. I'm not able to hear at this point. I don't know if anyone can hear me. This is Jim Castle --

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: -- counsel for Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Hello, Mr. Castle. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Good morning to you in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- your time in America. Thank you for appearing by this telephone conference. It was granted by a decision of 10 of December, 2007, and you are on the phone; is that correct, Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Yes, I am, and if I could address that for one moment. We had filed a waiver with the Court from our client, indicating he acceded to my request that I appear by teleconference and that he waived his appearance. We'll be following up with an additional waiver indicating that co-counsel will not be present also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you very much. I wanted to say the accused is not present. He is on provisional release, and his waiver of appearance originally was filed on the 14th of January, 2008. However, this waiver was referring to his representation by co-counsel, Mr. Novak Lukic. As Mr. Lukic is not present today, the accused will only be represented by you, Mr. Castle, via telephone conference. I understand this altered waiver will be filed in order to meet this concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before we go into pending motions, I would like to briefly address the health of the accused. The accused, Mr. Perisic, as I said before, is on provisional release, which was originally granted on 5th of June, 2005. He requested and was granted, on 6th of December, 2007, the 10th alteration of these conditions. The State of Serbia indicates he is in full compliance with all requirements. There are no issues, as far as the Chamber is aware, with respect to the accused's health or conditions of provisional release. Or would either party wish to discuss any matter and, for that purpose, to go into private session? Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: And on behalf of the accused, we have nothing to add. General Perisic is in good health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Castle. Now, as to item 2, pending motions, before discussing certain motions, a still pending matter is the filing of the second amended indictment. The Defence submitted its objections to this second amended indictment on the 11th of November, 2007, which was 30 days after they had received the B/C/S version. The Prosecution filed its submission, which is titled "A Response" but which the Defence refers to as a reply, on 22nd of November, 2007. This was within the time authorised by the Chamber. On the 3rd of December, 2007, the Defence filed a motion to strike the Prosecution reply, alleging it was out of time. In subsequent e-mail contacts, the Defence indicated it would withdraw this latter submission, but to date it has not done so. A draft of this decision is currently being reviewed by the Chamber. At yesterday's 65 ter conference, Mr. Castle, you were indicating again that the Defence will withdraw its "motion to strike." You were advised that it could be done orally at the status conference or it could be done in writing. May I ask you, Mr. Castle, if you wish to submit the withdrawal, and if so, if you wish to do so orally now or would prefer to make the submission in writing? May I advise --

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Yes, I would withdraw our objection orally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: -- and would state that based upon information that was provided to me by Mr. Harmon, it had indicated that in a previous status conference, Judge Robinson had provided more time to the Prosecution for its response than was normally authorised by rule. Therefore, our motion to strike was not well taken, and we would move orally to withdraw that motion to strike at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you. And may I advise the parties that a decision will likely be issued on this matter of the filing of the second amended indictment before the end of the month. Now, pending motions for discussion. (A) There is the Prosecution's motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts concerning Sarajevo. On the 6th of January, 2007, the Defence filed two responses. (B) Prosecution's supplemental 65 ter summary for witness Glasen Adamovic [phoen] of the 17th of August, 2007. The Defence's response was due the 31st of August, 2007. No response was filed. Is that correct? Yes. May I note that a decision will be taken in due course as it pertains to a Rule 92 ter/quater issue ordinarily taken by the Trial Chamber. (C) is the Prosecution motion pertaining to Rule 70. And (D), a Prosecution motion for leave to file a revised 65 ter list, with confidential annexes, filed on 22nd of October, 2007. This submission was followed by a further submission from the Prosecution, seeking to supplement the 65 ter list. The Defence filed a request for additional time to respond to this latter submission on 3rd of January, 2008, requesting a delay until there is a clarification as to what is contained in the ex parte annex, and further requests that the Prosecution be ordered to submit a detailed listing indicating the date on which each of their 514 documents added to the 65 ter list in the supplement were received. This matter is currently pending, and the Prosecution response is due on 17th of January, 2008, which is the day after tomorrow. Yesterday at the 65 ter conference, Mr. Castle agreed that the Defence submission is only a request for an extension of time to respond to the Prosecution's motion submitted on 19th of December, 2007, and does not encompass any response to the motion for leave to file the revised 65 ter list filed on 22nd of October, 2007. The parties were advised that the decision as to this list would take quite some time but that it may possibly be taken by the Pre-Trial Chamber if this Chamber is able to complete its work on this matter before the case is transferred to a Trial Chamber. However, this matter is not ready for a decision, as we are within the period for the Prosecution to file its response now, the 17th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, I'd like to inform the Court that following the court proceedings yesterday, I had a conversation with Mr. Castle. I don't know if Mr. Castle can hear me. Can you hear me, Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Castle, can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: I can hear Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Following the proceedings yesterday, I had a conversation with Mr. Castle in which I clarified the nature of the ex parte attachment B that was appended to the 19 December submission for additional -- identifying the additional exhibits. Furthermore, I sent to Mr. Castle, by e-mail, a dated -- a list of the 514 documents with the date that we had received each of those exhibits. What Mr. Castle and I discussed was attempting to resolve the matter without the necessity of filing a response. Mr. Castle will be reviewing the documents I submitted to him, and hopefully we may be able to make some progress. At least we will be able to report by the 17th, when our response is due, where we stand in that process. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Any comment, Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Well, yes. I agree with Mr. Harmon, since yesterday he did provide me information concerning the ex parte annex to their 65 ter amendment. I'm satisfied with the grounds for that. The additional -- the request in our motion for extension of time was in regard to learning from the Prosecution what -- or when they received the additional exhibits. They have provided that information to me, and I'm satisfied with that information. Ordinarily, the next step in the process would be for the Prosecution to reply on the 17th. However, there's very little to reply to at this point, because the Defence has requested an extension. The only thing that remains at this point is for the Defence to receive a copy of the exhibits. My understanding is that, well, originally they were sent, but there was a problem with the disc that was sent. So that has been re-sent as of either yesterday or today. It should be in my office within a week. My request of the Chamber would be to authorise the Defence until February 5th to file their objections and that the Prosecution would then have the ordinary amount of time to reply from that date. That would save a step in the process of the Prosecution filing a pro forma response on the 17th and the Chamber having to rule, accept orally at this time. That is our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Castle, that sounds reasonable to me. Mr. Harmon, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have informed Mr. Castle and the senior legal officer earlier that we had no objection to Mr. Castle's request for an extension of time. We would join in Mr. Castle's request, that extension until the 5th of February be granted. We would not file -- if that were to be the case, we would not file a written response on the 17th. We would wait to see the response, if any, by Mr. Castle. Perhaps in the interim time we can resolve this without the necessity of written pleadings and the Court having to make a decision, but we certainly join in Mr. Castle's request for an extension of time until the 5th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That is granted. Mr. Castle, you received that granting?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: I'm having some difficulty again hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Your request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: -- until the 5th of February. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: So the next thing, disclosure. We have the Rule 66 (A) (i). According to the work plan, the Prosecution should have complied with all of its obligations under this Rule at this point, so no issues should be arising. Is that right, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We have asserted many times that we have complied with that obligation, and the Defence has agreed that we have done so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: We would agree that they have complied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as to (B), Rule 66 (A)(ii). We have here: 1. According to the order establishing a work plan issued on 11th of October, 2006, the Prosecution should have complied with all its obligations under this Rule at this point. However, on the 12th of September, 2007, the Defence notified the Chamber that it had yet to receive the redacted statements of protected witnesses MP-003, MP-004 and MP-014. I will get back to that in a minute. 2. The Defence notified the Chamber, in the same 12th of September, 2007 submission, that it had not received the following materials falling within Rule 66 (A)(ii): (A) 14 witness folders which the Prosecution has indicated it would deliver in October. (B) prior testimony of either 102 or 104 priority witnesses. Only 59 have been received, and proofing notes have not been received. (C) statements of (redacted), John Almstrom and Milan Popovic. (D) Radislav Jovanovic and Lord David Owen, transcripts have been received, but proofing notes and prior statements have not been received. (E) Bogdan Sladojevic, testimony and transcripts from Dragomir Milosevic and an update of any other witnesses who may have testified since the initial disclosure. May I go through the rest - it's three other -- four other points - and then ask the parties to comment on that? Is that fine or would you now want to say anything? Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I leave it to your discretion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Castle, I had the impression it was some sound in the earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: We would agree with the Chamber's proposal. One other thing I would note is if -- with the permission of the Chamber, I'm wondering if Mr. Harmon -- my guess is he is rising every time he is speaking. I'm wondering if he could be excused from that requirement so that his voice is closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, that's a very good idea. Mr. Harmon, are you fine with that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm quite happy with that suggestion. Thank you. Is that better, Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: That sounds now better. I wanted to list the following sub-points: 3. The Defence also notified the Chamber that it had not yet received a B/C/S version of the transcript of the accused's statement. 4. At the status conference of 19th of September, 2007, the Chamber ordered the Prosecution to disclose the redacted statements of mentioned witnesses MP-003 and MP-004 within seven days. The Prosecution submission was that there was no witness statement provided by Witness MP-014. The Chamber declined to order the taking of a statement of MP-014 for the purposes of requiring its disclosure. 5. At the 65 ter conference yesterday, the Prosecution represented and the Defence agreed that the following matters listed above have now been disclosed: (A) the 14 witness folders which the Prosecution indicated it would deliver in October and;. (B) the B/C/S transcript of the statement of the accused. Now to the last point in this list, 6. As to the remaining issues, the Prosecution submitted the following: (A) As to those persons whom the Prosecution identified as "the French witnesses," apparently there are four in total, including (redacted) (redacted) and John Almstrom and two others. The Prosecution advised that they are currently engaged in a process required by the French government as a precursor to disclosure of these statements, and may I have -- and may have to address requests for protective measures for these individuals or their materials, should the French government so request. They are not yet disclosed. (C) As to Milan Popovic, the Prosecution submits that the Defence co-counsel, Mr. Novak Lukic, was present at the taking of a judicial statement taken at a hearing in Belgrade, and Mr. Novak Lukic was provided with a copy of that judicial statement at the time of the taking of that statement. (D) As to Lord David Owen, the Prosecution submitted, at the 65 ter conference, that there were no proofing notes or prior statements as to him. His prior transcript has been provided. However, today, at 10.48 in the morning, the Prosecution e-mailed the Defence counsel - it must have been quite early for you, Mr. Castle - with a copy to the senior legal officer, advising that the Prosecution had identified a court document and that they were immediately undertaking to disclose it. The Prosecution stated that Lord Owen only agreed to appear as a court witness and not as a Prosecution witness in the Slobodan Milosevic case and apparently intends to take the same approach in this case. But as he is on their witness list, the disclosures are required. (E) As to Vladislav Jovanovic, following the 65 ter conference on 14 January 2008, the Prosecution informed the senior legal officer that there are no statements or witness notes regarding this witness and that the transcript, which has been disclosed to Defence, is the only matter which the Prosecution has in its possession which requires disclosure. (F) As to Bogdan Sladojevic, the Prosecution submits that they have made all relevant disclosures from the Dragomir Milosevic case, including this witness's information. It appears that the disclosures are still pending as to the four French witnesses, but that the process is required to obtain approval from the French government as to these witness prior statements. As this case will shortly be ready to be transferred to a Trial Chamber, and as the disclosures under Rule 66 (B) should have been long ago completed in accordance with the work plan established on 11th of October, 2006, it would seem that more than a year later, the Prosecution should have informed the Chamber of this problem long before now. In order to move this process forward, as the Pre-Trial Judge, I order that the Prosecution, within 30 days, either to file a report concerning the process or to file a motion for protective measures, as requested by the French government, or a Rule 70 motion, or to disclose the materials. Thirty days are the 14th of February, 2008. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is understood, Your Honour. I just would like to make two points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: John Almstrom is not one of the French witness. He's a Canadian witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The same issues, I mean related issues, Rule 70 issues, apply to him. I am informed that there were verbal negotiations between previous counsel and Canadian officials, but I don't know the status of those ongoing or if they're -- the status of those negotiations. In respect of the 30-day ruling the Court just made, we don't have any problem with that. I will say, however, Your Honour, that we have informed the Court on previous occasions of the process, that there is a [French spoken] that is required, and the French government is working at a pace it deems appropriate. We have vigorously, vigorously made efforts to expedite the process. We have made multiple trips to Paris to ensure that the earliest possible compliance is done. So I think, fairly, the Prosecution has kept both the parties and the Court informed of this. We appreciate the Court's ruling, because we will convey that ruling to the French government, and hopefully we will be in a position within 30 days -- we will comply with one of the options that Your Honour has outlined. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, and I stand corrected if I got it wrong. I would clarify that the order applies to both the four French witnesses and Mr. Almstrom, whom I misrepresented as a French witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We understand, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you for your understanding. Now, a question to Mr. Castle. Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: I have nothing to add, and we appreciate the Chamber's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now as to (C), Rule 68, this disclosure of mitigating or exculpating material is an ongoing obligation anyway. These materials should already have been disclosed or will be disclosed as soon as noticed. Now, (D), Rule 66 (B). Just a moment. The Prosecution indicated that based upon the most current information it had, that it should be able to comply with the 31st of January, 2008, translation estimate they provided in the 31st of October, 2007 report. Other than noting this, I am advising the Prosecution that if it learns that it will not meet that deadline, they should notify the Chamber in a report and provide the reasons such translation cannot be completed in accordance with its estimated time. Further, they should provide a realistic estimate as to complete the outstanding 9.000 pages of translations. Now to (E), the Rule 94 bis expert reports. I will not take this issue up, but we should wait until Judge Robinson returns or the case is being transferred to a Trial Chamber. If the parties feel strong about it, they can seize the Chamber with a motion. Is that understood? Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Castle?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now to the pre-trial preparation, in the technical sense. We have (A), possible use of 92 bis/92 ter evidence. Here, motions will be dealt with by the Trial Chamber that will hear the case. The only issue is the filing of an additional request under Rule 92 quater, which does not require resolution in this hearing. Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I indicated yesterday, during the 65 ter conference, that we received notice of the unexpected death of a witness who was listed on our witness list. We intend to file a 92 quater motion based on that recent information and will do so as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes, understood. Mr. Castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: We'll await that request and respond accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Now as to (B), agreed facts, adjudicated facts and stipulations on the indictment. The parties filed a joint submission on agreements on matters of law on the 1st of May, 2007, and a joint submission on agreements on matters of fact on the 31st of May, 2007. As to adjudicated facts, Prosecution filed a motion for judicial notice concerning Sarajevo on the 6th of February, 2007, to which the Defence filed two responses. This motion is currently pending. On 23rd of May, 2007, the Pre-Trial Judge indicated that motions for admission of adjudicated facts should be determined by the Trial Chamber that will hear the case. Please, Mr. Castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Oops. I'm sorry, I couldn't hear that last statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I was just saying motions on adjudicated facts will be dealt with by the Trial Chamber that will hear the case. Could you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much now. Lastly, I would like to address the anticipated length of the trial and the trial date, in a brief form. On the 23rd of May, 2007, the Prosecution estimated that if none of its Rule 92 bis motions are granted and, "assuming that there is a sitting of five days a week in the normal course of business, with very few interruptions," the entire length of the trial will last a year and a half. I don't have to comment to that now. Just as to the date of the next meeting, it is anticipated that this case will be transferred to a Trial Chamber which will be assigned to hear the case in the very near future. A mid- to late spring start date is hoped for, and if the current projections hold, it is possible that this case should come to trial before the 120-day point, which would be the 14th of May, 2008. We will not set another status conference date, but advise the parties that if for any reason the case is not transferred prior to that date to a Trial Chamber, that they will be contacted to set the next status conference. Do the parties have any comments or any other matters? Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday, in the 65 ter conference, I raised the issue of my unavailability between the 3rd and the 13th of April and informed the senior legal officer as to the reasons why I would be unavailable. And I requested that the Trial Chamber, in setting a trial date, take that information into consideration. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. This is now on the record, and it can be worked on the basis of that information. Any other matters, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: No additional issues. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Then this status conference is closed, and we will get back to you as pointed out. Good afternoon. Good day to America.

utterances.speaker: MR. CASTLE
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good evening.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference concluded at
